notes: Korean root morphemes harvested from species-name pun etymologies. Each card teaches a Korean root that appears as a component of one or more Pokemon names. Opt-in via Settings > Etymology root cards.

auditFix.issue: 골아파 is not a single morpheme or noun meaning 'headache'. 고라파덕's pun decomposes as 골(이) 아파(요) 'my head hurts' — a phrase combining the noun 골 'head' with the predicate 아프다. The standalone Korean noun for headache is 두통. Tagging 골아파 as a 'root/morpheme' meaning 'headache' is a part-of-speech and morphological error.

기라스 in 마기라스 (Tyranitar), 데기라스 (Pupitar), and 애버라스 (Larvitar) is borrowed from 안기라스 — the Korean name of the kaiju Anguirus from the Godzilla franchise, which Tyranitar's line visually references. It is not a transliteration of the English suffix '-tar'. Tying the root to '-tar' obscures the kaiju reference and is etymologically wrong.

노고치 (Dunsparce) is not built from a meaningful 노고 'effort'. The Korean name is a transliteration of the Japanese ノコッチ, which itself is an anagram-style scramble of 츠치노코 (tsuchinoko, the Japanese cryptid the Pokemon is based on). There is no 'effort' morpheme in the etymology — teaching learners that 노고 means 'effort' here invites them to misparse 노고치.

entries.gloss: a great deal (colloquial); also lit. 10,000 steps (萬步)

auditFix.issue: 잠만보 (Snorlax) plays on 잠 'sleep' + 만보, but the morphemic punchline is the colloquial 만보 ~ 만큼/매우 'a great deal' (Snorlax sleeps and eats a great deal), reinforced by Japanese カビゴン. The literal Hanja reading 萬步 'ten thousand steps' is a real Korean compound (cf. 만보계 pedometer) but is not what 잠만보 is doing — Snorlax is famously sedentary, not a stepper. 'Countless steps' is the wrong sense.

entries.notes: From 알통몬 (Machop), 근육몬 (Machoke), 괴력몬 (Machamp), 시라소몬 (Hitmonlee) + 1 more

auditFix.issue: 샤 in 샤미드 (Vaporeon) is not an onomatopoeic 'water sound'. The widely cited Korean etymology is 샤워 (shower) + 머메이드 (mermaid). 샤 is a clip of 샤워 (English-derived 'shower'), a noun, not a water-sound mimetic. The current gloss invents an onomatopoeic reading.

entries.notes: From 거북왕 (Blastoise), 왕눈해 (Tentacool), 왕콘치 (Seaking), 왕구리 (Politoed) + 1 more

auditFix.issue: Cyndaquil (브케인) and Quilava (마그케인) are fire/storm hedgehog Pokémon whose Japanese names (ヒノアラシ Hinoarashi 'fire-storm', マグマラシ Magumarashi 'magma-storm') reference 嵐 'storm'. The Korean adaptation borrows from 허리케인 'hurricane' for the 케인 element — the file already contains a separate 허리케인 entry with this analysis. Glossing 케인 as 'cane/tail' contradicts both the Japanese motif (storm) and the established Korean fan analysis. 'Cane' (지팡이) and 'tail' have no support.

코리 in 코코리 (Phanpy) does not mean 'small'. 코코리 is built from 코끼리 (elephant) — the Pokemon is explicitly an elephant calf. The 코 of 코끼리 is doubled and clipped (코+코+리). Glossing the root as 'small' is invented; if anything the morpheme means 'elephant (clip of 코끼리)'.

Neither cited Pokemon supports 'cocoon-like body'. 콘팡 (Venonat) inherits from Japanese コンパン, where コン is from 'compound (eye)' (복안) — Venonat is a compound-eye gnat, not a cocoon. 쏘콘 (Forretress) uses 콘 from English 'cone' (Pineco/pinecone). A single gloss can't cover both, but 'cocoon-like body' fits neither.

entries.notes: From 니드킹 (Nidoking), 킹크랩 (Kingler), 잉어킹 (Magikarp), 야도킹 (Slowking) + 1 more

auditFix.issue: The single gloss 'sun' fits 해너츠 (Sunkern, from 해바라기 sunflower) and 해루미 (Sunflora) but is wrong for 왕눈해 (Tentacool), where 해 is a clip of 해파리 (jellyfish) — Tentacool is a jellyfish, not a sun. Lumping all three under 'sun' will mislead learners into parsing 왕눈해 as 'big-eye sun'.
